text: Everything so far in this course happens inside Snowflake. But a real production data platform is never just Snowflake — it's Snowflake plus a small set of tools that each do one job well around it.

Azure Data Factory moves raw data from source systems into Snowflake on a schedule. dbt transforms it with version-controlled SQL and tests. Python handles the logic that doesn't fit cleanly in SQL — API calls, scoring, custom branching. And Airflow coordinates all of it — sequencing, retries, alerting — without touching the data itself.

This is the detail that trips people up coming from on-prem ETL: in this stack, transformation isn't a separate server doing work before the data lands. It's SQL that Snowflake itself executes — usually generated by dbt — running on a Snowflake warehouse like any other query, billing credits the same way any query does.

A realistic run looks like this: Airflow kicks things off, Data Factory lands raw data in a staging schema, Airflow triggers dbt to transform staging into reporting views, a Python step enriches a dimension table through an external API, and Power BI queries the finished result. None of these tools compete for the same job — and overlap between them is usually a sign the stack was assembled without a plan.
Next lesson turns this into a decision framework: given a real scenario, which of these tools — or plain SQL — is actually the right one to reach for.
